newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan self-serve gas stands safe if staffed - report.
newsitem.headline: Japan self-serve gas stands safe if staffed - report.

text.p: Self-service gasoline stations, currently banned in Japan, could be operated safely if they were under the constant supervision of an attendant, the Fire Defence Agency said in a report.
It added that the attendant should have special knowledge about how to handle inflammable products and extinguish fires.

Self-service stations were banned in Japan for safety reasons, but under a three-year deregulation programme that began in April 1995, the Fire Defence Agency has been studying the dangers of self-service stations and the necessary safety measures.
The agency is due to make a decision by the end of March 1998 on whether to give self-service stations the go ahead.

The report said unmanned self-service stations were more dangerous than those with attendants, as there would be no guarantee that customers would refrain from smoking or turn off their automobile engines while filling their tanks.
The oil industry widely expects self-service stands to be approved and fears that an already vicious price war could escalate.
